examples.name: Default
examples.summary: Three cells with gutters between them — the `gap` register.

examples.name: Kinds
examples.summary: The same layout drawn three ways. In `divider` the seams are the grid’s own 1px gaps, so every cell must fill its own background; in `frame` each cell is a real frame box that draws its own rules and corner marks.

examples.name: Columns
examples.summary: Two column counts in one view — a count only reads against another.

examples.name: Balanced
examples.summary: Two, four and five cells under `columns: 3`. Every row is full: two split in halves, four make a 2 × 2, five make 3 + 2 with the last row sharing the width evenly. Pass `layout="fixed"` only for tiles whose width must not change from row to row.

examples.name: SeparatorColor
examples.summary: The muted hairline weight, for rules one step back.

examples.name: Frame
examples.summary: The framed register and everything its cell carries: the two fills, and an unpadded `kind="none"` cell whose content reaches the rules. Each cell draws only its right and bottom rules — the grid draws the matching top and left ones, so every edge is one hairline.
